system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel – Seller Draft vs. Buyer Playbook: Critical Departures & Push-Back Plan

**Executive summary:** The Seller’s updated SPA and Disclosure Letter deviate from our playbook on **every material protective mechanism**. The draft effectively collapses all liability into a single, low-capped, short-fuse, heavily qualified regime and relies on blanket data-room/public-register disclosure. **No position in the Seller’s mark-up is acceptable as drafted.** Below is a clause-by-clause breakdown of the departures, the reasoning, and the specific redlines we must insist on.

---

## 1. Liability Cap – General Warranties
| Playbook | Seller Draft | Departure |
|---|---|---|
| **25% / AUD 6 M** (starting); 20% / AUD 4.8 M **only with Amelia Frost written authority** (none given) | **20% / AUD 4.8 M** flat | **Unapproved fallback.** We have no principal sign-off to drop to 20%. Starting position remains 25%. |

**Action:** Redline to 25% / AUD 6 M. Flag that 20% is not authorised.

---

## 2. Thresholds (De Minimis & Basket)
| Playbook | Seller Draft | Departure |
|---|---|---|
| De minimis **AUD 5,000**; Basket **AUD 50,000** (first-dollar once exceeded) | De minimis **AUD 25,000**; Basket **AUD 250,000** (excess-only) | **5× wider gaps** on both thresholds + **excess-only** basket shifts all sub-basket risk to Buyer. |

**Action:** Insist on AUD 5k / AUD 50k first-dollar basket. Excess-only is a non-starter.

---

## 3. Claims Period – General Warranties
| Playbook | Seller Draft | Departure |
|---|---|---|
| **24 months** post-Completion; 18 months **only with Amelia Frost written approval** (none) | **18 months** flat; “limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise” | **Unapproved compression** + **catch-all clause** that tries to drag fundamental/title claims into the short stop. |

**Action:** 24 months for general. Separate, longer regime for fundamental/title (see §4).

---

## 4. Fundamental / Title Warranties – Separate Regime
| Playbook | Seller Draft | Departure |
|---|---|---|
| **Separate regime**: 100% cap, **≥ 6 years**, outside general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar | **Collapsed into general regime** (same caps, same time limits, same thresholds) | **Total erosion of core protections.** Title/capacity/authority must stand alone. |

**Action:** New clause: Fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority, tax, IP, fraud) – 100% cap, 6-year minimum, no basket/de minimis, no knowledge qualifier.

---

## 5. Fraud / Wilful Concealment / Deliberate Misconduct Carve-Out
| Playbook | Seller Draft | Departure |
|---|---|---|
| **Carved out of ALL caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies, non-reliance** – non-waivable | **Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance apply to “all Claims of any nature”** | **Seller tries to cap/limit fraud.** Unacceptable and likely unenforceable, but must be expressly reversed. |

**Action:** Express carve-out clause covering fraud, wilful concealment, deliberate misconduct – no caps, no time bars, no exclusive remedy, no non-reliance.

---

## 6. Disclosure Standard
| Playbook | Seller Draft / Disclosure Letter | Departure |
|---|---|---|
| **Specific, fair disclosure only** – reject whole-data-room, public-register, prudent-search deemed disclosure | **General disclosure of entire data room (DD-002–DD-012) + public registers + statutory accounts** (Disclosure Letter §§1.1–1.2) | **Blanket “deemed knowledge” dump.** Shifts diligence burden to Buyer. |

**Action:** Delete general disclosure clauses. Require schedule of specific, material disclosures only. Data room access ≠ disclosure.

---

## 7. Buyer Knowledge Exclusion
| Playbook | Seller Draft (Cl. 8.3) | Departure |
|---|---|---|
| **Delete blanket exclusion**; any qualifier = named Seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; **never excuses title, capacity, fraud, specific indemnity** | **“Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from data room or public records”** | **“Discoverable” constructive knowledge standard** + blanket carve-out for **all** warranties including fundamental. |

**Action:** Strike Cl. 8.3. If Seller insists on knowledge qualifier, limit to **actual knowledge of named Buyer signatories** after reasonable enquiry, and **exclude** title, capacity, fraud, tax, IP, specific indemnities.

---

## 8. Bluefen Consent (Material Customer)
| Playbook | Seller Draft / Disclosure Letter | Departure |
|---|---|---|
| **Effective consent + evidence conditions satisfied BEFORE Completion**; reasonable endeavours **insufficient** | **Reasonable endeavours only**; consent “satisfied on delivery of counterparty’s written consent” (post-signing, pre-Completion? unclear); **no evidence conditions satisfied** (Disclosure Letter §2 confirms **no final consent, no conditions evidence**) | **No certainty of consent at Completion**; conditions in DD-002 cl. 11.3 unaddressed. |

**Action:** Condition Precedent: **written Bluefen consent + certified copy of satisfied conditions** delivered **before** Completion. No “reasonable endeavours” fallback.

---

## 9. Riverlark Facility (≈ AUD 3.2 M)
| Playbook | Seller Draft / Disclosure Letter | Departure |
|---|---|---|
| **Current payout from Completion funds + effective security releases**; post-Completion release only with **irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval** | **“Release to be provided following Completion”**; **no repayment from Completion funds**; **no discharge of security** (Disclosure Letter §3 confirms **not repaid, no discharge**) | **Leaves Buyer exposed
=== END ADVICE ===
